mutation_rules.pattern: Y ↔ F ↔ W at peptide-contacting positions in CDR3
mutation_rules.rationale: Maintain π-π stacking with peptide aromatic residues while tuning stacking geometry and strength
mutation_rules.specificity_impact: May alter if peptide contact changes

examples.outcome: Reduced size, removed H-bond donor, improved stacking
Added H-bond capability, maintained aromatic stacking

when_to_use: Forms π-π stacking with peptide aromatic residue
cautions: Y→F removes H-bond donor capability
W is bulky, may cause steric clashes
May alter specificity if peptide contact geometry changes
contraindications: Low occupancy (<50%) - interaction may not be stable
No aromatic peptide residue nearby - stacking won't form

mutation_rules.pattern: R ↔ K, E ↔ D at peptide-contacting positions in CDR3
mutation_rules.rationale: Optimize salt bridge geometry by adjusting sidechain length and H-bonding capability

examples.outcome: Shorter sidechain improved salt bridge geometry

when_to_use: Salt bridge identified with moderate occupancy (50-80%)
Suboptimal geometry (distance >4.5 Å or poor angle)
cautions: R→K loses bidentate H-bonding capability
K→R may cause steric clashes if space limited
Charge optimization may affect specificity

mutation_rules.pattern: Introduce or optimize hydrophobic contacts (L, I, V, M) in CDR3
mutation_rules.rationale: Strengthen hydrophobic core at interface to increase binding energy
when_to_use: Hydrophobic peptide residue nearby (L, I, V, F, W, Y)
cautions: Avoid over-packing - may cause steric clashes
Hydrophobic residues on surface may reduce solubility
Large hydrophobics (W, F) may be too bulky

mutation_rules.pattern: Do not reverse charge (R→E, K→D, E→R, D→K)
mutation_rules.rationale: Charge reversal typically breaks favorable electrostatic interactions and introduces repulsion
when_to_use: Only if redesigning entire interaction network
cautions: High risk of breaking existing interactions
May introduce electrostatic repulsion
Difficult to predict outcome
contraindications: Existing salt bridge or favorable electrostatic interaction

mutation_rules.pattern: Do not introduce Proline in CDR3 loops
mutation_rules.rationale: Proline rigidifies loops and breaks backbone H-bonding, disrupting CDR3 flexibility needed for induced fit

examples.outcome: Rigidified loop, lost induced fit capability

when_to_use: Rarely - only if rigidification is specifically desired
May consider removing existing Pro if problematic
cautions: Proline breaks backbone H-bonding
Rigidifies loop structure
May prevent induced fit

mutation_rules.pattern: Avoid mutations in framework regions unless surface-exposed and non-critical
mutation_rules.rationale: Framework regions maintain structural integrity; mutations often destabilize fold or affect CDR positioning
cautions: High risk of destabilization
May affect CDR loop positioning
May reduce expression levels

mutation_rules.rationale: Single mutations have predictable effects; multiple mutations show unpredictable cooperativity
cautions: Multiple mutations may show cooperativity
Difficult to interpret failure of multi-mutants
Higher risk of destabilization

mutation_rules.rationale: Hotspot residues contribute most to binding energy; optimizing them has highest impact
cautions: Hotspots may be critical for specificity
Over-optimization may reduce cross-reactivity
Consider interaction type when designing mutation
contraindications: Low occupancy (<50%) - may not be true hotspot
Framework region - even if high RRCS

mutation_rules.pattern: High-flexibility regions (RMSF > 2 Å) tolerate mutations better
mutation_rules.rationale: Flexible regions can accommodate structural changes; rigid regions are constrained
cautions: High flexibility may indicate transient interactions
Check occupancy to confirm interaction stability
Rigidifying flexible regions may reduce induced fit capability

mutation_rules.rationale: Low-occupancy interactions are transient and may not contribute significantly to binding
cautions: Low occupancy may indicate transient or non-functional interaction
Check if interaction is present in dominant conformational cluster
Consider ensemble of conformations, not just average
contraindications: High RMSF with low occupancy (very transient)

mutation_rules.rationale: Extremely high affinity may impair T cell function by preventing serial triggering and rapid scanning

examples.outcome: KD = 0.5 nM, impaired T cell activation
KD = 10 nM, enhanced T cell activation

when_to_use: Test functional assays, not just binding
cautions: Too-strong binding may prevent TCR dissociation
May reduce serial triggering efficiency
May impair T cell scanning and activation
contraindications: Therapeutic TCR design - avoid KD < 1 nM

mutation_rules.pattern: Balance affinity enhancement with specificity maintenance
mutation_rules.rationale: Increasing affinity may broaden peptide recognition, reducing specificity

examples.outcome: 10x affinity, but increased cross-reactivity to off-target peptides

cautions: Affinity enhancement may reduce discrimination
Test binding to peptide variants
Consider biological context (polyspecificity may be beneficial)
contraindications: Single target peptide with no variants

workflow: Analyze interaction type (H-bond, hydrophobic, π-π, salt bridge)

specificity_tuning.goal: Improve discrimination between target and off-target peptides
workflow: Identify CDR3 residues contacting these positions
Design mutations optimizing fit to target, disfavoring variants
Test binding to target and off-target peptides
specificity_tuning.success_criteria: Maintained or improved target affinity, reduced off-target binding

stability_maintenance.goal: Preserve TCR structural integrity and expression
workflow: Test expression levels and structural stability (RMSD)
Consider stabilizing mutations (disulfide bonds, core packing)
stability_maintenance.success_criteria: Maintained expression, RMSD < 2 Å, no aggregation
